title: Reverse micellar extraction of recombinant cold-adapted AMS8 lipase
author: Fatin Nurfauziana

steps_raw.instruction: Preparation of recombinant cold-adapted lipase AMS8
The stock E. coli BL21 (DE3) containing pET32b/AMS8 plasmid is stored in 80 % (v/v) glycerol and kept at -80 °C
Streak the culture on the LB agar with ampicillin and incubated at 37°C, 12 h
Select one colony of E. coli and grow in LB broth with ampicillin (50 µg/ml), 37 °C for 16-18 h, and shake at 200 rpm
For another confirmation of lipase production, streak recombinant AMS8 lipase on Tributyrin LB agar plate containing ampicillin
Incubate the agar plate at 37 °C overnight and then, the plate transfer to 4°C for 1-3 days.
For the expression purposes, the single colony grow in LB broth (50 ml) containing ampicillin (50 µg/ml)
Add 100 mM of IPTG and incubate for 16-18 h
Harvest the bacterial cells into 50 ml falcon tube and centrifuge (6654 x g, 4 °C, 30 min)
Resuspend the cell pellets in 50 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM NaCl, pH 7
Sonicate for 6 min (intervals 30s off)
Centrifuge the cell suspension (6654 x g, 4 °C, 30 min) to separate supernatant (soluble lipase) and pellet (insoluble lipase)
Collect the pellet and treat with 8 M urea, 100 mM NaCl, and 10 mM CaCl2 for solubilization at 4°C for 1.5 h
Centrifuge the sample (6654 x g, 4 °C, 30 min)
For refolding method, titrate 50 mM sodium phosphate buffer, 100 mM NaCl, pH 7 to the sample with the flow rate 2 ml/min
Reverse micellar extraction (RME)
Prepare organic phase (Triton X-100 in toluene with different concentrations).
For the forward extraction, inject 10 ml refolded AMS8 lipase into organic phase (volume ratio 1:1)
Homogenize (601 x g, 15 min, 20 °C)
Centrifuge for phase separation (3000 rpm, 20 °C, 30 min). Emulsion is used for backward extraction
In the backward extraction, inject stripping solution (50 mM Tris-Cl, 1 M KCl, pH 9) into the emulsion and stir (601 x g, 30 min, 20 °C)
Centrifuge (3607 x g, 45 min, 20 °C)

Several parameters of RME were optimized to obtain better lipase recovery and extraction efficiency. In the forward extraction; initial aqueous phase (pH 5-9), surfactant concentration (0.01-0.09 M), salt concentration (0.075-0.175 M), and temperature (10-40oC). The lipase activity and protein content were estimated.
Dropwise 400 µl of 23.96 M pNPP solution into 3 ml of buffer solution (0.05 M sodium phosphate (pH 7), 0.1 g Arabic gum and 0.4 g Triton X-100) under strirring condition
Add lipase extract (50 µl) to reaction mixture and incubate at 20 oC for 5 min
Then, add 10 % (w/v) SDS solution to demulsify the reaction mixture (for organic phase)
Read at absorbance 410 nm
Estimation of protein content
Plot BSA standard curve in the range 0-2000 µg of protein
Add 1 ml of sample into 5 ml of alkaline copper reagent and vortex shortly
After 10 min, add 0.5 ml of 1 N Folin-Ciocalteu reagent and left for at least 20 min for detergent precipitation
Centrifuge (1202 x g, 10 min)
Read at absorbance 700 nm against a reagent blank

Estimation of protein content adapted from ChandraRajan & Klein (1975) using bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a standard [28]. BSA standard curve was plotted using protein solution in the range of 0-2000 µg of protein. The sample, 1 ml was added to 5 ml of alkaline copper reagent and vortexed to mix well. After 10 min, 0.5 ml of 1 N Folin-Ciocalteu reagent was mixed and left for detergent precipitate for at least 20 min. Then, it was centrifuged at 1202 x g for 10 min and the absorbance was measured at 700 nm against a reagent blank.

Precipitate sample from aqueous phase using 10% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) precipitation method
Prepare acrylamide gel : 12% (v/v) resolving gel and 4% (v/v) stacking gel
Mix 8 µl of lipase extract with 2 µl sample buffer and load into acrylamide gel
Run in a CriterionTM Vertical Electrophoresis Cell (USA) at 210 V and 60 mA for 1 h
Then, stain the gel for 5 min and destain using buffer solution of 0.05% (v/v) Coomassie Brilliant Blue G-250, 30% (v/v) methanol and 10% (v/v) acetic acid
A protein marker standard from Fermentas, USA and the molecular weight range is from 116.0 to 14.4 kDa.
Computational analysis
Protein sequence and predicted model of lipAMS8

Cold-adapted lipase isolated from Pseudomonas fluorescens strain AMS8 (GenBank accession no: ADM87309.1) was chosen as a template for molecular dynamic simulation. This predicted model AMS8 lipase was acquired by superimposing crystal structures of Serratia marcescens (GenBank accession no: 2qua) and Pseudomonas sp. MIS38 (GenBank accession no: 2z8x) due to their similar sequence identity [30].
Simulation parameters
MD simulation were accomplished on the predicted model of AMS8 lipase in the closed conformation with calcium ions and zinc ions intact
Open YASARA Structure (version 11.3.22, Krieger) software and load PDB file of your enzyme
Insert simulation box (choose: all around atoms)
Then, load 100 molecules of Triton X-100 molecules into the box by choosing other formats (sdf file).
Load toluene molecules into the box by set up densities according to the temperature.
Set up several parameters for respected experiments:
-Forcefield: AMBER03 with the cut off 10.846 Å
-temperature: 25 °C/ 298.15 K (can be set up for another temperatures)
-choose steepest descent minimization
Choose Edit and clean all the molecules
Before run for energy minimization, set the enzyme in the fix position
After completed the energy minimization, set the enzyme for the free position (record all the steps and final energy needed to complete energy minimization)
Then, save the scene as [your title.sce] format
Start run MD simulation for 10 ns
The analysis were measured by enzyme stability and flexibility at given simulated times by root mean square deviation (RMSd) and root mean square fluctuation (RMSf)
Align protein simulation snapshot in Triton X-100/toluene reverse micelles parallel arrangement (by superimpose) by using open source PyMOL Molecular Graphic System Version (https://pymol.org/2/)
